intro: Peterborough is a cathedral city on the River Nene in Cambridgeshire. On its western edge, beside Orton Hall in Orton Longueville, a broad path runs between two long lines of giant sequoias, the red-barked American giants that British estates planted in rows from the 1850s. A reader walked the avenue and sent us its biggest trunk, which they measured at almost six metres round.
meta_description: A giant sequoia in the avenue beside Orton Hall, Peterborough: a reader's tree, almost six metres round, and how to find it.

trees.story:
"A whole avenue of trees," is how the reader who sent us this sequoia described the place they found it, beside Orton Hall on the western edge of Peterborough.

Their photographs show what they mean. A broad earth path runs straight through the woods, and on either side of it stands a line of giant sequoias, their soft red trunks rising bare for a long way before the blue-green foliage begins. Ivy has climbed the nearest ones and browned in patches against the bark. This tree is the big trunk in the foreground on the left, thicker than any of its neighbours, and beyond it the line keeps going until the path disappears among the trunks.

Giant sequoias reached Britain in the 1850s, and this avenue followed fast. Parks and Gardens UK records that the Marquess of Huntly and his wife Maria, keen gardeners at Orton Hall, planted a 700-yard avenue of Wellingtonias, as the Victorians called them, along the estate's south boundary as seedlings in 1861.

The reader measured this one at 589 centimetres round and puts it at about 150 years old. Those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen; the planting date is the record's.

Walk the length of the path and look up as you pass each spire.

trees.access: The reader photographed it from the broad path through the avenue beside Orton Hall. We have not confirmed who owns the ground or when the path is open; check before you go.

trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-21 reader judge: sent by a reader through the app (b57c3977-d5d3-4a97-a199-76433a04d573). Photographs viewed: a double avenue of tall giant sequoias along a broad earth path, the nearest trunk thick, red and ivy-clad in the foreground; extras show the avenue running on, one sequoia whole from foot to spire, and the crowns from below. Summer daylight, colour. Published under the closed list for a reader's tree (Hidde, 2026-11-17). The reader's own figures: name 'Giant Sequoia near Bowthorpe', species 'Giant Sequoia', age '150', girth 589 cm; the site 'Orton Hall' and 'A whole avenue of trees' came in their report 1000107, filed on the Bowthorpe Oak by mistake of place (the app named the lead 'near Bowthorpe'). No register entry within 100 m, no encyclopaedia article within 300 m. Every figure on the page is theirs, except the planting date: a second reader-judge run the same afternoon found Parks and Gardens UK's record of the Orton Longueville Wellingtonia avenue (south boundary, seedlings planted 1861 by the 10th Marquess of Huntly and Maria), on which the photograph's location falls, and added it as the source.

question_meta: The giant sequoia avenue beside Orton Hall in Peterborough: where the biggest trunk stands and what we know about it.
question_answer: The Giant Sequoia of the Orton Hall Avenue stands beside Orton Hall in Orton Longueville, on the western edge of Peterborough, at the start of a long double line of sequoias along a broad earth path, planted as seedlings in 1861.
question_context: A reader who walked the path beside Orton Hall, in Orton Longueville on the western edge of Peterborough, sent us this tree and called the place "a whole avenue of trees". Their photographs show a broad earth path running straight through the woods with a line of giant sequoias on each side, their soft red trunks bare for a long way before the blue-green foliage begins, ivy climbing the nearest of them. The tree on this page is the thick trunk in the foreground on the left, much wider than its neighbours. Giant sequoias, Sequoiadendron giganteum, come from the western slopes of the Sierra Nevada in California and reached Britain in the 1850s. Parks and Gardens UK records that the 10th Marquess of Huntly and his wife Maria planted a 700-yard avenue of them along the south boundary of the Orton Hall estate as seedlings in 1861. The reader measured this one at 589 centimetres round and puts it at about 150 years old; those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen. We have not confirmed who owns the ground or when the path is open, so check before you go.

faq.q: Where is the giant sequoia avenue in Peterborough?
faq.a: Beside Orton Hall in Orton Longueville, on the western edge of the city. The tree on our page is the thickest, ivy-clad trunk in the line along the path.

faq.q: How big is the Giant Sequoia of the Orton Hall Avenue?
faq.a: The reader who sent it measured it at 589 centimetres round and puts it at about 150 years old. Those are their figures; we have not seen a published measurement. The avenue itself was planted as seedlings in 1861, by Parks and Gardens UK's record.

faq.q: Can I visit the Orton Hall sequoia avenue?
faq.a: The reader walked it on a broad earth path. We have not confirmed who owns the ground or when the path is open, so check before you go.
